newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan rates to rise in two years--Kajiyama quoted.
newsitem.headline: Japan rates to rise in two years--Kajiyama quoted.

text.p: Japanese government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama said Japan's interest rates will likely rise in the next one or two years as financial deregulation measures start taking effect, a financial daily reported on Sunday.

"Interest rates will go up by one or two percentage points one to two years from now after the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Control Law is revised and deregulation of the nation's financial markets proceeds," Nihon Keizai Shimbun quoted Kajiyama as saying.
"The interest rates' hovering at low levels contributes to making Japan competitive, among others," Kajiyama said.
Kajiyama made the remarks in a speech he gave on Saturday in Akita Prefecture, northeastern Japan.
